skills.name: vada-samvada
skills.description: Conduct bounded, constructive proposer–examiner dialogue with explicit questions, evidence, objections and graduation criteria.

skills.name: vaisheshika-description
skills.description: Analyze domain descriptions using Vaisesika distinctions among bearers, qualities, motion, universals, individuality, inherence and qualified absence. Use for conceptual modeling and category mistakes before formal encoding.

skills.name: nyaya-examination
skills.description: Examine contested claims using Nyaya knowledge-source distinctions, inference reconstruction, defeater checks and reasoned resolution. Use for consequential uncertainty or argument review, including an agent's self-review.

skills.name: evidence-grounding
skills.description: Link individual claims to exact source evidence while distinguishing source statements, observations, inference and verification.

skills.name: draft-refinement
skills.description: Revise a shared draft in response to justified objections and human feedback without hiding unresolved disagreement.

skills.name: rdf-formalization
skills.description: Encode examined meanings as RDF facts, ontology or constraints with a semantic round-trip explanation and explicit formalism boundaries.

skills.name: fact-extraction
skills.description: Extract source-grounded entity and relation assertions against an approved ontology without silently changing schema or identity.

skills.name: query-compilation
skills.description: Translate a natural-language question into an authorized query grounded in the actual ontology and entity bindings, then explain supplied execution results.

skills.name: research-result-check
skills.description: Check paired baseline and candidate measurements from an AI experiment, compute descriptive improvements across seeds, and draft a cautious result summary. Use for a quick sanity check of supplied results, not for running training or claiming statistical significance.

skills.name: skypilot
skills.description: Submit and inspect experiments on explicitly selected SkyPilot compute using Bash, synchronize code and data, collect artifacts, and manage the requested cluster lifecycle. Use for SkyPilot-backed CPU or GPU jobs on Kubernetes, Slurm, or supported clouds.
